title: How NEXUS answers a multi-hop question
subtitle: In development: dense search in Qdrant and graph traversal in Neo4j, fused into one context for a LangGraph agent.

nodes.label: User
nodes.detail: Asks something whose answer is spread across several connected facts, such as which suppliers of X are affected by Y.
nodes.tradeoff: Plain vector search finds similar passages but can't follow the links between them.

nodes.label: API
nodes.detail: Receives the question and returns the answer. FastAPI is the service layer in the planned stack.

nodes.label: Cache
nodes.detail: A Dragonfly cache is part of the stack to keep responses fast.

nodes.label: Ingest stream
nodes.detail: Text and structured data stream in through Redpanda and become both text chunks and graph entities.

nodes.label: LangGraph agent
nodes.detail: Orchestrates retrieval, chains the hops between facts, and writes the answer from the fused context.

nodes.label: Vector search
nodes.detail: Dense search finds the passages most similar to the question.

nodes.label: Knowledge graph
nodes.detail: Follows relationships from those passages to the facts they point at, which is what multi-hop questions need.

nodes.label: Fusion
nodes.detail: Merges the vector results and the graph results into one ranked context for the agent.

flow.text: Asks which suppliers of X are affected by Y.
Receives the question and passes it to the agent.
Starts retrieval for the first hop.
Finds passages similar to the question.
Follows relationships from those passages to connected facts.
Merges both result sets into one ranked context.
Chains the hops and writes the answer.
Gets an answer built from several connected facts.

takeaways.text: Vector search finds similar passages; graph traversal follows the links between them. NEXUS uses both.
Ingest turns the same documents into chunks for Qdrant and entities for Neo4j, streamed through Redpanda.
NEXUS is in development and private, so there are no results to report yet.
